title: Singular and plural nouns
summary: Most nouns add a silent -s in the plural: un livre → des livres, une maison → des maisons. You hear the plural in the article: les, des.
Nouns ending in -s, -x or -z do not change: un bus → des bus, un prix → des prix, un nez → des nez.
Nouns ending in -eau or -eu add -x: un gâteau → des gâteaux, un jeu → des jeux, un neveu → des neveux.
Most nouns ending in -al change to -aux: un animal → des animaux, un journal → des journaux. A few just add -s: des festivals, des carnavals.
A few nouns in -ail and -ou take -x: un travail → des travaux, un genou → des genoux, un bijou → des bijoux. Most others just add -s: des trous.
Irregular plurals: un œil → des yeux, monsieur → messieurs, madame → mesdames.
Some nouns are plural in French but singular in English: les cheveux (hair), les vacances (holiday), les devoirs (homework), les informations (the news).
In compounds made of an adjective + a noun, both parts take -s: des grands-parents, des petits-enfants. Un week-end → des week-ends.
When the noun is plural, the verb and adjectives change too: les châteaux sont beaux.

cards.front: How do most French nouns form the plural, and how can you hear it?
cards.back: Add -s, which is silent: un vélo → des vélos, une rue → des rues. You hear the plural in the article (les, des) and in liaison before a vowel: in les enfants the s is sounded like a z.

cards.front: What happens to nouns ending in -s, -x or -z in the plural?
cards.back: Nothing – they stay the same: un bus → des bus, un pays → des pays, un prix → des prix, un nez → des nez.

cards.prompt: Le matin, les ___ sont souvent en retard.
cards.en: In the morning the buses are often late.
cards.why: Nouns ending in -s, -x or -z don't change in the plural: un bus → des bus.

cards.front: What is the plural of nouns ending in -eau, -eu and -al?
cards.back: -eau and -eu add -x: un bateau → des bateaux, un cheveu → des cheveux. -al becomes -aux: un cheval → des chevaux, un hôpital → des hôpitaux. Exceptions that just add -s: un festival → des festivals, un pneu → des pneus.

cards.prompt: À la pâtisserie, j'ai acheté deux ___ au chocolat.
cards.en: At the cake shop I bought two chocolate cakes.
cards.why: Nouns ending in -eau add -x in the plural: gâteau → gâteaux.

cards.prompt: Mon petit frère passe trop de temps à jouer aux ___ vidéo.
cards.en: My little brother spends too much time playing video games.
cards.why: Nouns ending in -eu add -x in the plural: jeu → jeux.

cards.prompt: Il y a beaucoup d'___ à la ferme de mon oncle.
cards.en: There are lots of animals on my uncle's farm.
cards.why: Most nouns ending in -al change to -aux in the plural: un animal → des animaux.

cards.prompt: Mon grand-père lit deux ___ chaque matin.
cards.en: My grandfather reads two newspapers every morning.
cards.why: -al becomes -aux in the plural: un journal → des journaux.

cards.prompt: Cet été, nous allons à deux ___ de musique.
cards.en: This summer we're going to two music festivals.
cards.why: festival is an exception to the -al → -aux rule: it just adds -s (like carnaval → carnavals).

cards.front: Give the plural of: un œil, un travail, un genou, monsieur, madame.
cards.back: des yeux, des travaux, des genoux, messieurs, mesdames. Like genou, a few -ou nouns take -x (bijou → bijoux, chou → choux); most just add -s (un trou → des trous).

cards.why: œil has an irregular plural: yeux. French uses les for physical features: elle a les yeux bleus.

cards.prompt: Il y a des ___ dans ma rue, donc c'est très bruyant.
cards.en: There are roadworks in my street, so it's very noisy.
cards.why: travail → travaux (-ail → -aux). In the plural, les travaux often means building work or roadworks.

cards.prompt: Mon frère est tombé de son vélo et il s'est fait mal aux ___.
cards.en: My brother fell off his bike and hurt his knees.
cards.why: genou is one of the few -ou nouns that add -x: genoux (like bijoux and choux).

cards.front: Which everyday nouns are plural in French but singular in English?
cards.back: les cheveux (hair), les vacances (holiday), les devoirs (homework), les informations or les infos (the news). So the verb and adjectives are plural: Mes cheveux sont courts – My hair is short.

cards.prompt: Ma sœur a les ___ longs et bruns.
cards.en: My sister has long brown hair.
cards.why: Hair is plural in French: les cheveux (-eu adds -x). The adjectives are masculine plural too: longs, bruns.

cards.prompt: Le dimanche, je rends visite à mes ___.
cards.en: On Sundays I visit my grandparents.
cards.why: In an adjective + noun compound, both parts take -s: grands-parents, petits-enfants.

cards.instruction: Put the words in bold into the plural.
answers: J'ai acheté des cadeaux pour mes neveux.
cards.en: I bought presents for my nephews.
cards.why: -eau and -eu nouns add -x (cadeaux, neveux); un → des and mon → mes.

cards.instruction: Rewrite the whole sentence in the plural.
cards.why: château → châteaux (-eau + x); the verb becomes sont and beau → beaux.
